report:
### Conclusion
**Yes.** Offering HIV self-testing (HIVST) in addition to standard testing options causes more people to take an HIV test and increases overall testing frequency.

### Evidence
* **Increased Uptake:** Multiple systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) confirm that offering self-testing kits significantly raises the proportion of people who complete an HIV test compared to standard facility-based testing alone.
* **Reaching Priority Populations:** World Health Organization (WHO) synthesis of global data shows that HIVST reaches populations that standard clinic services often miss, including first-time testers, men, adolescents, and key populations who face heightened privacy or stigma concerns.
* **Bypassing Access Barriers:** By enabling individuals to test privately at a time and place of their choosing, self-testing bypasses major obstacles associated with healthcare facilities, such as fear of disclosure, long wait times, and transportation costs.
* **Higher Testing Frequency:** Evidence demonstrates that access to self-testing increases overall testing frequency among higher-risk groups, encouraging routine monitoring rather than infrequent, single-event testing.

Because of this strong body of evidence, the WHO explicitly recommends HIV self-testing as an additional strategy to expand testing coverage.

### Sources
* WHO Evidence Update: https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/WHO-CDS-HIV-19.36
* Lancet Systematic Review: https://www.thelancet.com/journals/eclinm/article/PIIS2589-5370(21)00271-6/fulltext
* NIHR Evidence Alert: https://evidence.nihr.ac.uk/alert/self-testing-kits-increase-overall-hiv-testing-uptake-in-men-who-have-sex-with-men/
* Meta-Analysis of RCTs: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40621547/
